traits.stem_clump.note: Imagekit woody-forms photo tally (2026-10-19, plantgen-claude project-files/image-data/woody-forms-2026-10-19/TALLY.md): two or more stems from at or near the ground (multiple) in 6 of 8 photo votes, lost 1, kept 1.

traits.leaf_area_per_basal_area.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 27 bigleaf maples: 0.191 m² of leaf a cm². Median leaf area over trunk area at breast height of its open-grown street and park trees 20 cm or more through, the trees the broadleaf median (0.167) was taken over.

traits.crown_spread.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 30 bigleaf maples 25 years or older (Longview, WA): 0.67 (quartiles 0.55 and 0.79). Median crown width over height of its trees 25 years or older (15 or older where it has fewer than 10 that old), measured open-grown street and park trees.

traits.crown_base_share.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 30 bigleaf maples 25 years or older (Longview, WA): 0.15 (quartiles 0.13 and 0.19). Median height of the crown's base over the tree's height of its trees 25 years or older (15 or older where it has fewer than 10 that old), measured open-grown street and park trees, which are often pruned up for clearance.

traits.branch_posture.note: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, p. 688): 'stout often pendulous branches forming a compact handsome head'.

traits.leaf_colour_autumn.note: Wikipedia, Bigleaf maple (read 2026-10-18): "In autumn, the leaves turn gold and yellow". Colour ours.

generator.params.sprout_light.note: A choice of the model's (leaf life, generator revision 44): a dormant bud sprouts in at least 0.55 of the open sky's light (sapindaceae's 0.25). Once a leaf stayed one season, not two, more light reached the inner crown, more dormant buds sprouted, and the open crown outgrew the module limit between 120 and 180 years; at 0.55 it peaks at 0.64 to 0.79 million modules (0.86 million before) and keeps its reference heights and dbh.

traits.flowering_months.note: iNaturalist research-grade records on GBIF in the south and central Puget Sound lowlands (46.7 to 48.0° N, 122.0 to 123.1° W; counted 2026-10-14): 176 records annotated as flowering (Mar 19, Apr 149, May 7, Jun 1); stated as the months holding at least a tenth of them, March and April. FEIS (Acer macrophyllum) gives late April to early May for the Pacific Northwest.

traits.fruiting_months.note: USA National Phenology Network observations (Nature's Notebook) at lowland sites west of the Cascades in Washington and Oregon (below 300 m, west of 121.8° W; 2009 to 2026, fetched 2026-10-14): 92 plant-years at 51 sites seen with ripe fruit, by the months they were seen in (Jan 4, Feb 1, Mar 1, Apr 1, May 6, Jun 10, Jul 33, Aug 31, Sep 43, Oct 29, Nov 23, Dec 8); stated as the months with at least a third as many as the busiest, July to November. FEIS (Acer macrophyllum): seeds ripe from August to October and shed from October to January, some staying on the tree until March; so ripe samaras are on the tree from August to January.

traits.height_max_m.note: Jepson (1925), as A. macrophyllum: grows 9.14 m to 28.96 m tall (converted from feet).

traits.wood_modulus_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, Maple, bigleaf, green: modulus of elasticity 7,600 MPa in static bending (clear wood, centre-loaded, span 14 depths; specific gravity 0.44).

traits.wood_rupture_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, Maple, bigleaf, green: modulus of rupture 51,000 kPa (clear wood in static bending).

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Acer macrophyllum (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.47 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 5 records in 4 sources); trunks 0.48, branches 0.47. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: The Woody Plant Seed Manual (Acer, table 2, read): minimum seed-bearing age 10 years. FEIS (Fryer 2011, read): bigleaf maple first produces seed when about 10 years old. It sets adult_age through the rule at the seed plants (spec rework P6), in place of the 10 years set by hand.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from photographs of open-grown trees: a broad, dense, rounded crown about as wide as it is tall; a short trunk that leans and divides low into three stems; opposite buds; leaves on long petioles about 0.3 m across, and leaf area per card matched to the drawn leaf. Not fitted to measurements. Growth plan G1 (2026-10-08): grown by the `sapindaceae` program (terminal flowering forks the shoots; shoots rise; space renews where limbs are shed, and limbs that no longer pay their way are shed) to 250 years (typical life 50-200 years, feis-acemac; "well over 200" in the San Juan Islands, islandhistories), with keyframes spaced roughly geometrically (and 30 years, the age ivy grows on it). Its architecture follows Scarrone's model: terminal racemes fork the shoots (Acer pseudoplatanus is Scarrone in Legner et al. 2013; see plantgen/forms/G1-ARCHITECTURE.md). Open-grown crowns are about as wide as the tree is tall and trunks 0.6-2 m dbh (feis-acemac); leaf blade 15-30 cm wide on a 15-25 cm petiole (kpu-plantdb), which the 0.4 m card with a 0.42 petiole share matches. Fitted 2026-10-08 against the Urban Tree Database (see allometry) and Joshi's photographs of open-grown trees: the crown's height (crown_height 26, height_rate 0.038) to the database's heights by age; its width (crown_radius 9.5, crown_rate 0.027) toward feis-acemac's open-grown trees, "generally as wide-spreading as they are tall", and photographs of open-grown trees, which show a dome as wide as tall or wider (2026-10-23: at crown_radius 6.5 it drew a column twice as tall as wide; the Urban Tree Database's open-grown broadleaves 45 to 70 years old are 0.6 to 0.9 as wide as tall); crown_base 2.5 lets the lower crown reach down toward the ground; space_density 30, space_kill 0.4 and space_reach 1.8 so shoots fill the crown finely enough that it reads as dense from the side (about 10 to 15 % see-through in plantc renders); one leaf pair a year on a short shoot (spur_pairs 1), which also keeps leaf area per crown area near the database's 6 to 7.5 m²/m²; its trunk is the pipe model's, from the broadleaf trees' rules (no ring rate). Each plant draws its own crown: radius within 30 % and height within 25 % of the envelope's (crown_vary, height_vary). The database's 30 trees over 20 years old scatter about its fitted curves with a standard deviation of 0.15 in log height and in log crown diameter, nearly independently (r = 0.13), which uniform draws within 26 % and 27 % match; crown_vary is a little wider for the broad open-grown forms. Its widest point lies within 0.1 of the crown's depth either way. Billows (crown_bumps 0.2, crown_bump_size 4 m) are set by eye from photographs of open-grown crowns, whose surfaces are mosaics of foliage domes a few metres across; at 0.3, narrow crowns grew overhanging lobes. Short shoots leaf out only in at least 0.15 of the open sky's light (spur_light, broadleaf's 0.1), which trims leaves deep in young crowns. Known gap: crowns still hold more leaf per crown area than the database's (1849 m² on a 16.6 m crown at 120 years, 8.6 m²/m², against 2117 m² on 18.9 m, 7.5). The database estimates leaf area from photographs, and this tree's leaves are at the top of the species' size range: a 0.4 m card draws 470 cm², against a mean of 280 cm² in feis-acemac. Crown height 25.5 m (was 26) since broadleaf revision 17 (woody forms, 2026-10-17), when buds stopped shading like leaves and its tallest plant grew past the greatest 28.96 m. Its crown's width is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured width over height of open-grown trees of its lineage (crown_spread, USDA Urban Tree Database) since 2026-10-23, in place of a hand-set crown_radius. Its crown's base is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured share of the tree's height below its crown (crown_base_share, USDA Urban Tree Database), and its stem divides only where its flora or photographs say its leader is lost or that it stands on several stems, since 2026-10-24, in place of hand-set crown_base and fork values.

allometry.note: USDA Forest Service Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005, public domain): its fitted age-to-dbh and dbh-to-height equations for bigleaf maple in the Pacific Northwest region (Longview, WA; 40 open-grown park and street trees aged 1 to 150 years), evaluated at 30, 50, 75 and 120 years. The same equations give crown diameters of 10.7, 14.4, 17.0 and 18.9 m and leaf areas of 594, 1034, 1483 and 2117 m², which the crown's height (crown_height, height_rate) was fitted to; its width is set wider for trees grown in the open (see generator.params).

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs. Leaf: five deep, sparsely toothed lobes on a long petiole. Bark: shallow twisting ridges, a buttressed base and moss on the upper side of thick limbs, as on coastal trees. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: hanging racemes of paired samaras about 4 cm long, green and bristly at the seed. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: hanging racemes of yellow-green flowers in April; samaras green all summer, brown in September and October, falling into the winter. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth when young, then grey-brown and shallowly furrowed into narrow interlacing ridges; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Leaf families (plant roadmap P4, `families`): sun leaves smaller and more deeply lobed than the large thin shade leaves inside the crown; set from general knowledge of sun and shade leaves and juvenile foliage, not measured. Shade colour (foliage_shade, 2026-10-08) about 0.7 of the sun colour: a leaf's colour moves toward it with the shade it grows in, and most leaves of a dense crown sit in a fifth of the open sky's light or less. With the old shade colour, 0.4 of the sun colour, plantc side renders drew the crown at 0.08 of the sky's brightness, against 0.29 to 0.36 in four photographs of open-grown trees.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

appearance.organs.bloom.season.flower_lo.note: Its flowers drawn one by one (spec rework L1b): small fragrant yellow-green flowers about 6 mm across in long hanging racemes. From general descriptions of the species (OregonFlora, the Flora of North America and nursery and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read). The size is the flower's width, or a closed corolla's length, over the fruit's length, roughly as in life. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): five yellow-green petals between five sepals, eight stamens and a pistil of two carpels, from the characters of Sapindaceae and Acer by the rules at the flowering plants.
